merger_description:
Idameneo (No. 123) Pty Ltd as trustee for the Artlu Unit Trust (trading as ForHealth) (**ForHealth**) proposes to acquire the business and operating assets comprising the Mackay Family Medical Practice clinic (the **Target**) from Health and Care Pty Ltd as trustee of the Health and Care Unit Trust (the **Acquisition**).   

  

ForHealth operates a network of over 100 multi-service medical centres (including 61 dental centres which are primarily co-located in the ForHealth medical centres) across New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, South Australia, Australian Capital Territory and Western Australia. ForHealth’s multi-service medical centres include general practice (**GP**) services as well as a range of other medical and allied health services.   

  

Mackay Family Medical Practice is a clinic providing GP services in Mackay, Queensland. Post-acquisition, ForHealth intends to continue operating the site as a GP clinic offering the same services.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application and market
share, the ACCC considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise
to any material lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between ForHealth and
Mackay Family Medical Practice in the supply of general
practice medical services in the local area surrounding the
Mackay Family Medical Practice
b. there are alternative providers of general practice medical
services in the local area surrounding the Mackay Family
Medical Practice.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
